$description: Single source of truth for McKesson data-visualization design tokens. Edit here, then run `python tokens/build.py` to regenerate every platform file in dist/. Brand values extracted from the McKesson Social Media Guide (2023/24) and FY26 Impact Report (2026); data-viz roles are this kit's own.

blue.description: McKesson Blue. Primary brand color; default single-series fill; 'focus' color.

navy.description: McKesson Navy. Chart headlines, totals, benchmarks, and the highlight accent (used where other brands would reach for orange).

orange.description: McKesson Orange. A brand color, but internally used only when it carries meaning (negative, below target, the low end of a diverging scale). Never as decoration or a plain highlight: executives read it as a warning.

deep_navy.description: Dominant dark in the FY26 Impact Report; dark slide / card backgrounds.

extended.$description: Extended Audience Palette. Each family maps loosely to a business area, but any color may be used in data viz. Order within a family: light, mid, base, dark.

amber.usage: Not used internally. Do not use in charts. Its base appears only as the at-risk status color (color.status).

brand.proportion_rule: Use the core palette for ~80% of a piece and one audience color for ~20% (McKesson Standard Template). Workforce Innovation uses the teal family, as in the template's infographic slides.

title.description: Slide titles: Bold, McKesson Blue, as in the McKesson Standard Template.

primary.description: Subtitles, data labels, body. 8.1:1 on white.

muted.description: Axis ticks, footnotes, source. 4.7:1 on white (AA).

dark.description: Dark slides / dim rooms / social cards.

grid.description: Gridlines, only when needed (lighter than axis).

context_light.description: De-emphasized fills in stacks/areas; masked columns.

focus.description: Primary highlight against grey context; default single-series fill. The color used most.

focus_light.description: Light-blue series fill for the 'uniform + accent' pattern (the navy exception pops against it); secondary series.

accent.description: The one exception that must pop (navy): against a light-blue series, or next to a blue focus group. Orange is never the accent.

positive.description: Better / favorable (McKesson green). Green vs. orange is not color-blind safe on its own: always pair with a symbol (▲ ▼) or words.

positive_text.description: Green for text and thin marks on white (5.4:1).

negative.description: Decrease / loss / below target (orange). The one job orange has in charts. Blue-orange is CVD-safe; avoid red-green.

categorical.$description: The McKesson Standard Template's infographic colors, ordered by how McKesson actually uses them (owner, 2026-10-04): blue, navy, bright blue, teal, mint; orange is the last-resort 6th and otherwise means 'worse'. Use the first N; prefer <= 4, and at 5 or more consider small multiples or group the tail into 'Other' (context grey). Green is not a category color: it means 'better' and 'on track'. Blue and navy sit side by side in stacks: keep the white separators.
categorical.$fill_tints: Light tints for large fills only (never lines or text), outside the series order.

steps.$description: Ordered stages in process infographics (pipelines, journeys, timelines), blue to green as in the template. Not for data magnitude (use sequential) or for unordered categories.

status.$description: Status (RAG) only: trackers, roadmaps, scorecard status columns, as in the template's Initiative Tracker. Never for data series. Always pair the color with a symbol and a word.

orange_blue.description: Negative (orange) to positive (blue) with warm-neutral midpoint. CVD-safe.

social.$description: High-contrast three-tone combos for social / single-KPI cards (background + 1-2 foreground).

family.fallback_web: 'Libre Franklin', 'Franklin Gothic Book', Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif
family.source: Open-source (SIL OFL) via Google Fonts or BrandHQ. Install locally for Office; load from Google Fonts for HTML.

roles.$description: size_px for screen/HTML at 1x; size_pt for 16:9 slides (13.33 x 7.5 in). Never go below the 'footnote' size.

slide_title.note: Slide (or page) title: the insight for the whole slide. Bold, McKesson Blue, 24-28 pt (the template's 34 pt is for short titles; insight titles run to two lines). With one chart on the slide, the chart's headline IS the slide title.

headline.note: Chart headline: the insight of one chart, SemiBold, full sentence, <= 2 lines. Used when a chart has its own title (two charts on a slide, reports, dashboards, chart images).

subtitle.note: Neutral chart title: metric, unit, scope, period.

tick.note: Axis tick labels and category labels.

annotation.note: Callout body; callout title uses bold.

kpi.note: Big-number callouts, Bold so the number pops.

typography.slide_title_style: Insight slides: the whole title Bold (slide_title role). Covers, section dividers and guide page titles only: the brand signature, bold lead word(s) + light remainder, e.g. '**Stacked** bar chart'.

bar.note: Bar width ~2x the gap between bars.
